chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Clara Smith and Perry Bradford's recording of Mamie Smith
summary: Danny recalls Clara Smith's low-down blues, and how the relentless Perry Bradford finally got Crazy Blues recorded; Milt helped bury him. End of Tape 5 side A.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Clara Smith was a defiant little dark woman. She sang the low-down Blues. There was Clara, and Mamie and Bessie, that trio. Trixie... There was just a whole slew of Smith sisters. As long as you had name Smith, you could put that on the marquee... I don't know if I mentioned it before. They just put that big name of Smith, and people took it for granted that it was...
Old Perry Bradford handled them for a while, didn't he.
Perry Bradford recorded the first Blues singer, which was Mamie...
The first Black woman on record.
Yeah. He went from record company to record company (there wasn't but four of them then), and nobody

would accept it. Finally, one of the guys broke through and let him record, and they recorded his tune, "The Crazy Blues." And that swept the country.. And he was a smart... He was a relentless little man. I mean, there was no such thing as trying to tell him "That can't be done."
Yeah, he stayed right with it.
Right to the end. I was with him when he died, Danny. He was that way when he died!
I understood you was responsible for burying him. You don't mention that...
Yeah, that's true. Well, we got him a place and kept our eye on it. But he was...
